thread:
Marta R: Heads-up — getting a customer escalation: sustained 503s since 09:12 UTC after the 08:50 deploy. Customers reporting timeouts and partial responses. Seeing repeated upstream runner exits in logs.

Josh L: Can you paste the error lines?

Marta R: Logs show GPU OOM followed by SIGSEGV and container restarts. Example: ```
[2026-03-16T09:11:58Z] infer-runner[pid=4217]: cudaGetLastError: out of memory
[2026-03-16T09:11:58Z] infer-runner[pid=4217]: === Caught signal 11 (Segmentation fault) ===
[2026-03-16T09:12:00Z] kubelet: container restart count=3
```

Kevin T: Is this happening across the pool or single host?

Marta R: Appears to be a subset of nodes in us-west1-pool-b. Restart spike correlates with high batch-size for a particular customer route (/v1/generate).

Amelia S: @sre-oncall-bot can you pull recent pod OOM/killed events and GPU memory metrics for that pool?

sre-oncall-bot: pulled metrics for us-west1-pool-b (09:00-09:20 UTC): average GPU mem util jumped from 62% -> 98% on 4/12 nodes. Pod kills: 12. Top processes by GPU mem: infer-runner (quantized-opt-epoch).

Josh L: Did the 08:50 deploy include any model/runtime change?

Marta R: Yes — we pushed commit 8f3a2 with a prefetch change in KV cache + a new attention kernel path for small-seq perf. Rollout was to 30% then auto-targeted more nodes due to traffic.

Kevin T: Possible regression: prefetch could be increasing KV cache residency and combined with kernel path may spike activation memory. Need quick repro.

Amelia S: Support Escalations, can you contact the customer and ask for a request sample + batch size they're sending? Also gather a sample trace id.

Support Escalations: Reached out to customer at 09:18 UTC — they sent a sample request + trace id trace-9a3f. They confirm batched requests of 8 at ~512 tokens typical.

Marta R: Repro steps I'm running locally against the canary image: 
1) deploy canary image 8f3a2 to a single node
2) send 50 concurrent /v1/generate requests with batch_size=8 and seq=512
3) watch nvidia-smi and runner logs

Josh L: Can you dump the runner config for that canary? env and flags?

Marta R: Runner flags: `--max-batch-tokens=8192 --kv-prefetch=on --attention-tile=small` and using quantized model q8_0. Memory limit set to 28GB (node has 40GB).

Kevin T: If the limit is 28GB and actual mem usage spikes to ~36GB due to combined activations + cache, the kernel will OOM the process. Two mitigation options: 1) revert the prefetch toggle 2) increase pod mem limit or pin that customer to a lower-memory model variant.

Amelia S: For immediate mitigation: recommend rollback of the KV prefetch flag for the Canary rollout and patch the rollout to stop expanding until we confirm memory profile. Can we do a quick rollback?

Josh L: I'll open a deploy revert PR and trigger a rollback to 8f3a1 (pre-change). If deploy takes ~5m, we should see reduced OOMs.

Marta R: Also adding a temporary routing rule to divert traffic from affected nodes -> fallback pool (cpu-surge-fallback) to reduce customer impact.

sre-oncall-bot: routing update applied: diverted ~12% of traffic for customer X to fallback pool at 09:27 UTC.

Support Escalations: Customer confirmed latency improved after diversion but still seeing occasional 503s. They want ETA for fix.

Kevin T: Root-cause hypothesis: KV prefetch increased per-request KV cache footprint; combined with new attention kernel increases peak GPU scratch. Under batched concurrent load we exceed pod mem limit causing gpu OOM -> SIGSEGV.

Marta R: I've started a controlled repro on a staging node with profiling enabled (cuda-memstats). Early snapshot shows per-request KV ~600MB when prefetch on vs 120MB off.

Josh L: Great. Let's proceed: 1) rollback canary (in progress) 2) patch rollout to set kv-prefetch=false by default until we optimize cache eviction 3) create a follow-up to make kernel path memory-safe (cap scratch usage).

Amelia S: I'll update the incident playbook and notify SRE pager. Also tagging eng-runtime for a deeper perf/memory audit.

Marta R: Postmortem notes to collect: affected customer IDs, exact pod names, gpu memory dumps, trace ids, PRs for rollback, and timeline.

Support Escalations: Customer updated at 09:41 UTC: "Thanks — errors mostly cleared after your mitigation. We'll keep an eye and report anything else." :thumbsup:

Kevin T: After rollback stabilizes, schedule a canary with mem-profiling and lower traffic. Add an alert for sudden per-pool GPU mem jump (>80% and restart rate >3 in 10m).

Josh L: Rollback completed at 09:33 UTC. Restart count trend dropping. Monitoring shows fewer OOMs. I'll keep the revert PR open until postmortem completed.

Marta R: Thanks everyone. Follow-up owners: Kevin (root-cause investigation), Josh (rollback + PR), Amelia (customer comms + playbook update). We'll reconvene 11:00 UTC for postmortem draft.

sre-oncall-bot: Incident marked as mitigated at 09:44 UTC — continuing to monitor."
